key_insight: D-Gun-sprayed NiCrAlY delivered greater hardness and corrosion resistance, while 80Ni20Cr achieved lower erosion mass loss on Al 6061-T6.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection should match the dominant damage mechanism: NiCrAlY for hardness and saline corrosion resistance, or 80Ni20Cr for the tested particle-erosion condition.
method: Deposited 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 using detonation-gun thermal spraying.
Characterised microstructure, phases, roughness and hardness using SEM-EDS, XRD, AFM and nanoindentation.
Evaluated saline corrosion, wettability and solid-particle erosion.
evidence_signal: NiCrAlY reached 7895.36 MPa hardness versus 780.11 MPa for 80Ni20Cr, with corrosion rates of 0.00567 and 0.01427 mm/year, respectively, versus 0.5185 mm/year for bare aluminium.
watch_item: Results are laboratory-specific; corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature and erosion testing at 90°, 40 m/s for 5 minutes do not establish long-term service life.
paper_title: Microstructure and surface performance of detonation gun sprayed 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 substrate for structural applications
